t: QGroundControl: What QGroundControl Is: The Pilot's Screen
title: QGroundControl: What QGroundControl Is: The Pilot's Screen
description: QGroundControl is the window into the uncrewed vehicle: a cross-platform app (desktop, tablet, phone) showing the map, the vehicle's position and attitude, live telemetry (battery, link, GPS), video from the onboard camera, and the controls to plan missions, tune parameters, and command flight. It speaks MAVLink to PX4 and ArduPilot. The GCS is where the human's judgment meets the vehicle's autonomy — the most safety-critical screen in the operation.

t: QGroundControl: Mission Planning: Patterns and Corridors
title: QGroundControl: Mission Planning: Patterns and Corridors
description: QGC's plan view builds missions visually: waypoints, survey grids (with camera triggering computed from overlap settings), corridor scans, and structure scans — with terrain-aware altitudes and battery-aware feasibility estimates. The plan shows distance, time, and photo count before upload. Planning well is the operation: a good plan makes the flight boring, and boring is safe.

t: QGroundControl: Telemetry: Reading the Vehicle's Health
title: QGroundControl: Telemetry: Reading the Vehicle's Health
description: QGC's fly view is the health dashboard: attitude indicator, altitude, speed, battery (voltage, current, remaining), GPS status, link quality, and mode — plus the message feed where the vehicle reports events. Reading it fluently is the operator's core skill: the battery trend says more than the battery number, and a degrading link margin is the warning before the failsafe. The pros watch trends, not snapshots.

t: QGroundControl: Parameters: Tuning from the Ground
title: QGroundControl: Parameters: Tuning from the Ground
description: QGC's parameter editor exposes the autopilot's hundreds of settings with documentation, grouping, and safe ranges — plus the tuning UI for the common gains. Changing parameters over the radio is powerful and dangerous: the discipline is one change at a time, recorded, with the old value noted for rollback. QGC's parameter diff and backup tools exist for exactly this.

t: QGroundControl: Your First Connection: USB to Telemetry
title: QGroundControl: Your First Connection: USB to Telemetry
description: The hello-world: plug the flight controller into USB, open QGC, watch the vehicle appear — parameters download, the map centers, telemetry flows. Then the radio: SiK telemetry modules paired, baud rates matched, link established. The beginner's lesson is the link budget: USB is infinite, radio is precious, and the stream rates should reflect that.

title: QGroundControl: Video: The Operator's Eyes
description: QGC streams the onboard video — RTSP or UDP — alongside telemetry, with recording. The video is the operator's eyes for inspection, search, and landing judgment. The engineering is bandwidth: video competes with telemetry on the same link, so the stream budget (resolution, bitrate) is set deliberately, with telemetry protected. A frozen video is an information failure the operator must notice — hence the age indicator.

title: QGroundControl: Geofences and Rally Points
description: QGC's safety planning: polygon geofences (inclusion and exclusion), rally points as emergency landing spots, and RTL altitude — drawn on the map, uploaded with the mission. The geofence is the contract the autopilot enforces; QGC is where the contract is authored. Drawing the fence around the actual hazards (not just the legal boundary) is the operator's judgment call.

t: QGroundControl: Defensive Uses: The Accountable Operation
title: QGroundControl: Defensive Uses: The Accountable Operation
description: QGC's defensive value is operational accountability: every plan versioned, every command logged, every parameter change recorded — the mission as an auditable artifact. In programs where flights are reviewed, QGC's logs (telemetry plus the operator's actions) are the record. The GCS is also the safety interlock: geofences authored here are enforced by the vehicle, and the plan review is the human gate.

t: QGroundControl: Multi-Vehicle: Fleet on One Screen
title: QGroundControl: Multi-Vehicle: Fleet on One Screen
description: QGC handles multiple vehicles: the map shows the fleet, the operator switches focus, and missions upload per vehicle. Fleet operations add the coordination questions — separation, tasking, comms — but the GCS pattern scales: one screen, many vehicles, each with its own telemetry and link state. The discipline is attention: the GCS shows all, the operator prioritizes.

t: QGroundControl: Debugging: Link and Data Issues
title: QGroundControl: Debugging: Link and Data Issues
description: GCS debugging classics: no connection (baud rate, driver, cable), parameters that will not download (link too weak for the burst), telemetry dropouts (stream budget exceeded), video that will not start (codec/pipeline). The ladder is physical (cable, power), then link (baud, pairing), then software (versions, settings). Half of GCS problems are cables — check the cable first, with dignity.

title: QGroundControl: Customization: Branding and Workflows

Done well, the custom GCS enforces the program's procedures instead of just permitting them.

t: QGroundControl: Firmware Updates Through the GCS
title: QGroundControl: Firmware Updates Through the GCS
description: QGC flashes firmware: PX4 and ArduPilot builds for the connected board, stable or custom, with the ritual every operator learns — backup parameters, flash, restore, verify. The GCS is the fleet's update tool, and the discipline is staging: one vehicle, test flight, then the fleet. A bad flash grounds aircraft; a staged flash grounds one.

t: QGroundControl: Testing: GCS in the Loop
title: QGroundControl: Testing: GCS in the Loop
description: GCS software is tested like flight software: against SITL vehicles, with scripted operator workflows, and with link fault injection (drop the telemetry mid-mission — does the GCS show it honestly?). The GCS must never show a confident lie: stale data must look stale, lost links must look lost. Testing the GCS means testing its honesty under failure.
